proposals.relationship: Tosh acknowledges Davidoff’s jointly authored Family Fortunes as an inspiration and historical resource for the Manful Assertions project.
proposals.evidence_note: Own 2023 retrospective p.178 and n.3 explicitly acknowledge both coauthors. The 2020 edited conversation, published 2023, pp.301–302 supplies a qualification: the group knew Family Fortunes but pursued men’s history as a totality and was less attentive than it could have been to multiple gender positions. This is a bounded debt for the shared 1991 project co-edited with Michael Roper; it is not sole authorship, complete adoption or a claim of chronological causal priority from co-presence.

proposals.relationship: Tosh draws on Foucault’s diagnosis of the present through the different world of the past to frame the public relevance of masculinity history.
proposals.evidence_note: Own 2023 chapter pp.179–180 explains the diagnostic purpose of history of the present and its relevance to histories of masculine crises. It is a specific retrospective conceptual resource, with an immediately stated reservation, not proof of Tosh’s original formation. Note11 cites Discipline and Punish, Alan Sheridan translation, Vintage1995, pp.30–31; that translation is not independently read.

primary_locators.passage: Foucault discussion, continuing over page break, note11 p.185.

proposals.relationship: Tosh questions the confinement of Foucault’s history of the present within academic discourse and proposes history for the present addressed to a lay public.
proposals.evidence_note: Own chapter p.180: after recognizing Foucault’s relevance, Tosh states his reservation that Foucault did not consider reaching a lay readership and that subsequent practitioners seldom prioritize this. Criticism concerns public address, not a blanket rejection of genealogical analysis or a claim that Foucault wrote no public interventions. Foucault’s cited text remains mediated through Tosh’s stated reading.

primary_locators.passage: Paragraph beginning The aspiration; reservation and proposed change of preposition.

proposals.relationship: Tosh uses Scott’s claim that representations of the past construct gender in the present as a starting point for developing history addressed to lay audiences.
proposals.evidence_note: Own chapter p.181 identifies Scott’s statement as foundational and then insists that productive public engagement requires more than the assumption: the priorities of lay readers may reset scholarly direction. The qualified use is retained in one resource edge; it establishes neither complete agreement nor a newly discovered original debt. Note14 identifies Gender and the Politics of History (1988), p.2; Scott’s book itself is not freshly read.

primary_locators.passage: Paragraph beginning In one of the foundational texts; note14 p.186.

proposals.relationship: Tosh invokes Davis’s call to study women and men within the whole system of gender relations to justify masculinity history as part of feminist inquiry.
proposals.evidence_note: Fresh selected original-article opening p.179 read through Paperzz OCR, browser lines34–51. Tosh expressly identifies Davis’s 1975 response, interprets its relational power argument and makes the gendered study of men indispensable to feminist historical work. This is a demonstrated conceptual use, not merely a reference; the original Davis address remains unread and the OCR is not image-collated.
